redesign_directions.task: Write a complete new program (replacing the EVOLVE-BLOCK) that reads the input, initializes the grid to the original map, and runs simulated annealing for the time limit. Moves: pick a random cell, change its color to 0 or to a color of an adjacent cell. Accept the move if all colors 0..m remain connected (non-empty) and all pairwise adjacencies match the original; otherwise reject. Use a temperature schedule that starts high and cools, accepting worsening moves with probability exp(-delta/T) to escape local optima. Maintain edge counts between colors and use BFS for connectivity checks. Output the best grid found.
redesign_directions.hypothesis: The current algorithm only erodes wards that originally touch the border. By allowing cells to be recolored to adjacent colors (not just 0), a non-border ward can give a cell to a border-touching neighbor, which then erodes it to 0, effectively shrinking the interior ward without creating illegal 0-adjacencies. A simulated annealing search over the full color assignment can explore these boundary movements and potentially shrink all wards to minimal skeletons, significantly increasing the number of 0 cells.
